title: The text discusses the history and evolution of the Kamajors, a civil defense militia formed in Sierra Leone during the early 1990s to protect communities from violence. Initially created to combat the Revolutionary United Front (RUF), the Kamajors faced mistrust and animosity from the army, especially after the suspicious death of their leader, Dr. Alpha Lavalie. Following a military coup in 1997, the Kamajors disbanded but later regrouped to fight for the reinstatement of the democratically elected government. As the political situation evolved, many Sierra Leoneans fled to Guinea, where they established new lives and businesses. However, with the restoration of democracy, many are returning home, leading to mixed emotions and challenges as they leave behind a life of relative comfort. The text highlights the complexities of exile, return, and the ongoing struggles faced by those still in Guinea due to ongoing violence in Sierra Leone.
